prose.detail:
The prototype defines 15 germinal-product commodities (Cattle Semen 05111000, Cattle Embryos/Ova 05119985, and the same pairs for Cat, Dog, Goat, Horse, Pig, Sheep, plus Rabbit/Rodent Semen), each flagged `isGerminalProduct: true` ([[c1]]) and each with `packagingFields: []` and its own reduced certification-purpose list ([[c2]]). [[c3]] concatenates them into `allCommodities`, and [[c4]] makes the combined set searchable specifically for the design-release-2.1 session.

A single grep for `germinal`, `netWeight` or `packageType` across the whole of the frontend's live-animals set returns exactly one hit — an email sentence in [[c5]]. The frontend's commodity data ([[c6]]) has no germinal entries and its COMMODITY_TYPE_DATA carries no such flag.

This one gap is the root of three separate downstream findings in this band (germinal quantity fields on Commodity details, germinal identifier set on Identification details, the Temperature question and certification-purpose suppression on Additional details). It is listed as its own increment because those three cannot land until a commodity can be marked as a germinal product at all. The design decision: whether germinal products are in scope for the live-animals service at all, or belong to a separate notification type.

CORRECTED DURING VERIFICATION: Two traces of germinal products DO exist in the frontend, just outside the grepped path/terms, and neither weakens the finding: [[c7]] (PACKAGE_COUNT_COMMODITIES) names semen and embryo/ova commodities such as '05111000 - Semen - Cattle' and '05119985 - Embryos/Ova - Cattle', and [[c8]] carries a 'Germinal products' certification purpose. Neither is a selectable commodity and neither carries a germinal flag, so the class remains unrepresentable — but 'no concept of' should read 'no selectable germinal commodity and no germinal flag'.

FALSIFIED BY: A decision record placing germinal products out of scope for this service, or any `isGerminalProduct`-equivalent flag already present in the frontend's commodity model.

The seed fans review.placeOfOrigin out across placeOfOrigin, consignor, consignee, importer and placeOfDestination ([[c1]]), and the review view model shows that same address for four of them ([[c2]]). But the list card for the same template advertises Consignee 'Glen Keen Farm' and Consignor 'Rice Lane City Farm' ([[c3]]) — two different parties. The captured screens show both halves of the contradiction: [[c4]] has the differing card values, [[c5]] has one address repeated four times. Acorn Farm disagrees with itself the same way: card origin 'Republic of Ireland' ([[c6]]) against review countryOfOrigin 'France' ([[c7]]) and a Romanian place of origin ([[c8]]). The card fields and the template body are simply not derived from one another. That matters because the frontend has no shared-address concept to inherit: each party commits its own {name, address} snapshot under its own key ([[c9]]), and the picker re-finds the source record by name within that role's book ([[c10]]). What IS comparable, and is a real gap, is the hand-off contract. Prototype: `setAddressBookConsignmentReturn` stashes the section id, path, heading and a suggested address type ([[c6]]); on completion it writes the address into the section's session keys — i.e. pre-selects it — and sets a success message ([[c7]], specifically 7808 and 7817), which the picker renders as a `govukNotificationBanner` ([[c8]]). prose.detail:
The two forms are field-for-field equivalent (frontend [[c1]] vs prototype [[c2]] — same nine fields, only the internal name prefixes and two label wordings differ), so the 29 mechanical deltas on this pair are overwhelmingly naming noise. The real difference is what happens on submit. The frontend builds `privateTransporterRecord(values)` and commits it into journey answers ([[c3]]) — one-shot, per-notification, never reusable. DR2.1's `saveAddedTransporter` ([[c4]]) unshifts the record onto `sessionData.addedTransporters` so it appears in the /transporter table on every subsequent notification (surfaced via getAllTransporters, [[c5]]), and when the flow was entered from the address book it also writes an address-book entry under `category: 'transporter'` ([[c6]]). DR2.1 therefore treats private transporters as reusable party records; the frontend treats them as free text.

The nine fields themselves are the same set, and the submit-behaviour claim — the substance of the finding — is fully verified.
